deep.reconstruction:
The page records two numerical values. They belong to the lemniscatic theta-function computation on the previous page (15r). There Gauss uses four functions P, Q, p, q of an argument measured in degrees. P is a pure sine series, P = (1) sin x + (3) sin 3x + (5) sin 5x + ... . The four functions satisfy:
- the quartic relations pp = QQ - PP and qq = PP + QQ;
- the duplication formulas P(2x) = 2PQpq and Q(2x) = P^4 + Q^4 = (p^4 + q^4)/2, with similar formulas for p(2x) and q(2x).

The values at x = 90° stated on 15r are P(90°) = Q(90°) = (1/2)^(1/4), p(90°) = 0 and q(90°) = 2^(1/4). This page converts them to decimals:
(1) P(90°) = Q(90°) = 2^(-1/4) = 0.8408963 [correct value 0.84089641...].
(2) q(90°) = 2^(1/4) = 1.1892071.

Why the first value matters (my gloss): putting x = 90° into the sine series gives sin(n·90°) = 1, 0, -1, 0, ... . So P(90°) = (1) - (3) + (5) - (7) + ... . This is the alternating-sum evaluation Gauss wrote on 15r: (1) - (3) + (5) - ... = (1/2)^(1/4). This page is therefore a clean numerical restatement, probably for comparison with the numerically computed coefficients. 15r also gives a separate partial-sum value, (1)-(5)+(9)... = 0.8393264.

Consistency check (mine): at 90° with P = Q we get pp = QQ - PP = 0, so p = 0. We also get qq = 2PP = 2·2^(-1/2) = √2, so q = 2^(1/4). Both agree with the stated values.
errors: 0.8408963 should be 0.8408964 to seven decimals, since 2^(-1/4) = 0.840896415... . The last digit is truncated or slipped rather than rounded. Only a minor numerical slip.

results.what: Special values of the lemniscatic theta-type functions at the quarter period: P = Q = 2^(-1/4), q = 2^(1/4), p = 0, with decimal evaluation
results.modern_name: special values of theta functions for the lemniscatic modulus (k = 1/√2), e.g. θ-quotients at half-period
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (lemniscatic researches, c. 1797–1800, Nachlass, Werke III); later published theory by Jacobi (1829)

results.what: Alternating sum of the sine-series coefficients of P equals 2^(-1/4) (evaluation of the series at 90°)
results.modern_name: evaluation of theta series at a quarter period

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only two decimal evaluations of fourth roots, continuing the well-documented Gauss Nachlass work on lemniscatic theta functions. Nothing new.
